row_statement: Conjecture 4.1 of Li and Yuan (for a prime n > 3 with ord_n(3) odd and r = (n-1)/ord_n(3), the number of cyclic codes over F_3 of length n with no full-weight codeword equals the sum of binom(r,j) for 0 <= j <= r/2) is false at n = 109, where ord_109(3) = 27 and r = 4: the family of shift-invariant subspaces of F_3^109 with no all-nonzero vector has at most 9 members, while the formula gives 11. Lean proves the bound for actual submodules, with the factorization of X^109 - 1 into irreducibles proved inside Lean; the exact value 9 is not claimed in Lean.

caveats: The true count 9 equals the lower bound 3^(r/2) of the source's own Theorem 4.2; the new input is two explicit full-weight words found by a quick structured search. The conjecture extrapolated from the single case n = 13.
109 is the first eligible prime after 13 with r >= 4; the source tested 11 and 13 only.
The journal's typeset version was not read; the public manuscript (arXiv v1, the only version) still has the conjecture.
